summary: @onereach/step-voice preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a large obfuscated sibling script
details: The package's npm `preinstall` script runs `setup.mjs`, which either invokes a locally-installed `bun` or downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun` releases, extracts it, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute `math_init.js` — a 727KB heavily obfuscated file using an obfuscator.io-style shuffled string array (`WV8StW` rotation, large `n7gIxM` constant table) and hex-named identifiers with a `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle header. `math_init.js` sits at the tarball root outside the `package.json` `files` allowlist (which declares only `/dst`), and the declared `main: index.js` is absent from the tarball, so the package's only effect on `npm install` is the execution of the obfuscated blob under an alternate runtime. The file name (`math_init.js`) does not correspond to the package's advertised purpose (voice steps). Using a downloaded alternate runtime to auto-execute an obfuscated, undeclared payload at install time matches the alternate-runtime-dropper attack pattern, evades Node-based scanners, and prevents static review of what the payload actually does on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
